entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-f5wc-c3c7-36mc: golang.org/x/crypto doesn't drop invoking agent constraints when forwarding keys
entry.content:
golang.org/x/crypto doesn't drop invoking agent constraints when forwarding keys

Aliases: CVE-2026-39832, GO-2026-5006

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • golang.org/x/crypto — fixed in 0.52.0

When adding a key to a remote agent constraint extensions such as restrict-destination-v00@openssh.com were not serialized in the request. Destination restrictions were silently stripped when forwarding keys, allowing unrestricted use of the key on the remote host. The client now serializes all constraint extensions. Additionally, the in-memory keyring returned by NewKeyring() now rejects keys with unsupported constraint extensions instead of silently ignoring them.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-vgwf-h737-ff37: golang.org/x/crypto: Invoking client can cause server deadlock on unexpected responses
entry.content:
golang.org/x/crypto: Invoking client can cause server deadlock on unexpected responses

Aliases: CVE-2026-39830, GO-2026-5017

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • golang.org/x/crypto — fixed in 0.52.0

A malicious SSH peer could send unsolicited global request responses to fill an internal buffer, blocking the connection's read loop. The blocked goroutine could not be released by calling Close(), resulting in a resource leak per connection. Unsolicited global responses are now discarded.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2025-4155: Excessive resource consumption when printing error string for host certificate validation in crypto/x509
entry.content:
Excessive resource consumption when printing error string for host certificate validation in crypto/x509

Aliases: BIT-golang-2025-61729, CVE-2025-61729

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.24.11, 1.25.5

Within HostnameError.Error(), when constructing an error string, there is no limit to the number of hosts that will be printed out. Furthermore, the error string is constructed by repeated string concatenation, leading to quadratic runtime. Therefore, a certificate provided by a malicious actor can result in excessive resource consumption.

References:

  • https://go.dev/cl/725920
  • https://go.dev/issue/76445

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-4870: Unauthenticated TLS 1.3 KeyUpdate record can cause persistent connection retention and DoS in crypto/tls
entry.content:
Unauthenticated TLS 1.3 KeyUpdate record can cause persistent connection retention and DoS in crypto/tls

Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-32283, CVE-2026-32283

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.25.9, 1.26.2

If one side of the TLS connection sends multiple key update messages post-handshake in a single record, the connection can deadlock, causing uncontrolled consumption of resources. This can lead to a denial of service. This only affects TLS 1.3.

Inefficient policy validation in crypto/x509

Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-32281, CVE-2026-32281

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-4339: Arbitrary file write using cgo pkg-config directive in cmd/go
entry.content:
Arbitrary file write using cgo pkg-config directive in cmd/go

Aliases: BIT-golang-2025-61731, CVE-2025-61731

Affected:

  • toolchain — fixed in 1.24.12, 1.25.6

Building a malicious file with cmd/go can cause can cause a write to an attacker-controlled file with partial control of the file content. The "#cgo pkg-config:" directive in a Go source file provides command-line arguments to provide to the Go pkg-config command. An attacker can provide a "--log-file" argument to this directive, causing pkg-config to write to an attacker-controlled location.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2025-4014: Unbounded allocation when parsing GNU sparse map in archive/tar
entry.content:
Unbounded allocation when parsing GNU sparse map in archive/tar

Aliases: BIT-golang-2025-58183, CVE-2025-58183

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.24.8, 1.25.2

tar.Reader does not set a maximum size on the number of sparse region data blocks in GNU tar pax 1.0 sparse files. A maliciously-crafted archive containing a large number of sparse regions can cause a Reader to read an unbounded amount of data from the archive into memory. When reading from a compressed source, a small compressed input can result in large allocations.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-4337: Unexpected session resumption in crypto/tls
entry.content:
Unexpected session resumption in crypto/tls

Aliases: BIT-golang-2025-68121, CVE-2025-68121

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.24.13, 1.25.7, 1.26.0-rc.3

During session resumption in crypto/tls, if the underlying Config has its ClientCAs or RootCAs fields mutated between the initial handshake and the resumed handshake, the resumed handshake may succeed when it should have failed. This may happen when a user calls Config.Clone and mutates the returned Config, or uses Config.GetConfigForClient. This can cause a client to resume a session with a server that it would not have resumed with during the initial handshake, or cause a server to resume a session with a client that it would not have resumed with during the initial handshake.

References:

  • https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/K09ubi9FQFk
  • https://go.dev/cl/737700

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-5037: Inefficient candidate hostname parsing in crypto/x509
entry.content:
Inefficient candidate hostname parsing in crypto/x509

Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-27145, CVE-2026-27145

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.25.11, 1.26.4

(*x509.Certificate).VerifyHostname previously called matchHostnames in a loop over all DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. This caused strings.Split(host, ".") to execute repeatedly on the same input hostname. With a large DNS SAN list, verification costs scaled quadratically based on the number of SAN entries multiplied by the hostname's label count. Because x509.Verify validates hostnames before building the certificate chain, this overhead occurred even for untrusted certificates.

References:

  • https://go.dev/cl/783621
  • https://go.dev/issue/79694
  • https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/tKs3rmcBcKw

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-w5pg-649r-p6gg: Gitea: Branch Protection Bypass via PR Retargeting Preserves Stale `official` Approval Flag
entry.content:
Gitea: Branch Protection Bypass via PR Retargeting Preserves Stale `official` Approval Flag

Aliases: CVE-2026-58439, GO-2026-6080

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • code.gitea.io/gitea — fixed in 1.27.0

## Summary Gitea does not re-evaluate the `official` flag on existing pull request reviews when a PR's target branch is changed. An attacker with write access to a repository can obtain an `official: true` approval on a PR targeting an unprotected branch, then retarget the PR to a protected branch (e.g., `master`). The approval, which would have been `official: false` if submitted against the protected branch, is preserved and satisfies the protected branch's required approvals, allowing the attacker to merge without legitimate maintainer approval. - Confirmed on Gitea **1.25.4** (`1.25.4+41-g96515c0f20`) ## Vulnerability Details ### Root Cause When a review is submitted on a pull request, Gitea computes the `official` flag by checking whether the reviewer is in the **target branch's*…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-4864: TOCTOU permits root escape on Linux via Root.Chmod in os in internal/syscall/unix
entry.content:
TOCTOU permits root escape on Linux via Root.Chmod in os in internal/syscall/unix

Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-32282, CVE-2026-32282

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.25.9, 1.26.2

On Linux, if the target of Root.Chmod is replaced with a symlink while the chmod operation is in progress, Chmod can operate on the target of the symlink, even when the target lies outside the root. The Linux fchmodat syscall silently ignores the AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW flag, which Root.Chmod uses to avoid symlink traversal. Root.Chmod checks its target before acting and returns an error if the target is a symlink lying outside the root, so the impact is limited to cases where the target is replaced with a symlink between the check and operation.

References:

  • https://go.dev/cl/763761
  • https://go.dev/issue/78293
  • https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/0uYbvbPZRWU
